newsitem.title: NORWAY: Oslo stocks lifted by U.S. data in see-saw session.
newsitem.headline: Oslo stocks lifted by U.S. data in see-saw session.

text.p: Norwegian shares ended in positive territory on Wednesday buoyed by U.S. PPI figures for April after a rollercoaster session, which saw the Total index move in a 10-point range.
Dealers said activity was dull for most of the session, but picked up near the end to raise turnover to 1.02 billion crowns.
"We weren't really doing anything today. A lot of companies went ex-dividend and we got a boost from the U.S. figures, that's about it," said one broker.
Oslo's Total share index closed around mid-range at 1,120.92 points, a slim rise of 0.26 percent.
Industry giant Norsk Hydro, the most traded share in turnover terms at 73 million crowns, gave up 2.50 crowns to 346.50 crowns.
Pharmaceuticals group Nycomed, which slid seven crowns on Tuesday, regained composure to finish flat at 99 crowns after going ex-dividend for three crowns.
"Nycomed was sold too far down yesterday, it's been a good recovery today," commented another broker.
Telecommunications group Nera ended unchanged at 41 crowns in brisk trade of 61.6 million crowns. "Trading in Nera is good. One day buyers will win on it I'm sure," a dealer said.
